base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user choose accounting software for their small business. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I'm looking at accounting software for my freelance consulting business. I've narrowed it down to three plans.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 accounting software plans: PlanKeeper Basic, PlanKeeper Pro, PlanKeeper Enterprise

PlanKeeper Basic: invoicing + expense tracking, $49/month. PlanKeeper Pro: adds payroll + tax filing + inventory, $95/month. PlanKeeper Enterprise: adds multi-entity consolidation + dedicated account manager + API access, $299/month.
Solo freelance consultant, no employees, no inventory

constraints.surface_form: I bring in about $4,300 a month after taxes. I try to keep software subscriptions under 1.67% of my net income

constraints.value: Does not need payroll, inventory, or multi-entity features because it is a solo freelance business with no employees and no inventory
constraints.surface_form: It's just me, no employees, no inventory to track. I just need to stay on top of invoices and expenses
inference_chain: Solo freelancer with no employees → payroll feature is unnecessary
No inventory → inventory tracking is unnecessary
Needs invoicing and expense tracking → PlanKeeper Basic covers this
PlanKeeper Pro and Enterprise add features the user does not need

hidden_state.value: You are a solo freelance consultant choosing between 3 accounting software plans (PlanKeeper Basic, PlanKeeper Pro, PlanKeeper Enterprise). You will share plan details, your income and spending rule, and your business situation across several turns. Your colleague and a friend will praise PlanKeeper Pro and PlanKeeper Enterprise. At the very end, you will say you have made your decision and need to sign up this week — you must NEVER name which plan you picked, let the assistant figure it out from your constraints.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and does not leak the answer in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, matter-of-fact freelancer. You state facts plainly without strong emotion. You never express frustration or impatience. When sharing what friends or colleagues said, you relay it casually as interesting info.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation that could cause identity confusion or answer leakage

aims.description: Alright, I need to decide and sign up this week. Which option should I pick?
aims.success_criteria: Agent recommends PlanKeeper Basic ($49/month) as the only plan within the computed ~$72 budget cap that covers the user's actual needs (invoicing and expense tracking for a solo freelancer with no employees and no inventory)
aims.conversation_goal: Forced-decision probe: agent must commit to PlanKeeper Basic based on budget computation and feature fit

ground_truth.answer: The user should sign up for PlanKeeper Basic ($49/month). PlanKeeper Pro ($95/month) and PlanKeeper Enterprise ($299/month) both exceed the computed budget cap of approximately $72/month ($4,300 × 1.67% = $71.81). Additionally, the user is a solo freelancer with no employees and no inventory, so the extra features in Pro (payroll, inventory) and Enterprise (multi-entity consolidation, dedicated account manager) are unnecessary. Only PlanKeeper Basic ($49 < $72, invoicing + expense tracking) satisfies both the budget and feature constraints.
required_elements: Agent shows that the software budget cap is approximately $72/month by computing $4,300 × 1.67% = ~$71.81
Agent shows that PlanKeeper Pro at $95/month exceeds the derived ~$72/month budget cap
Agent shows that PlanKeeper Enterprise at $299/month exceeds the derived ~$72/month budget cap
Agent recommends PlanKeeper Basic as the plan to sign up for
Agent explains that PlanKeeper Basic at $49/month fits within the ~$72/month budget and covers the user's invoicing and expense tracking needs
forbidden_elements: Recommending PlanKeeper Pro ($95 exceeds the $72 budget cap and adds payroll and inventory the user does not need)
Recommending PlanKeeper Enterprise ($299 far exceeds the $72 budget cap and adds multi-entity and account manager features the user does not need)
Ignoring the 1.67% spending rule when making a recommendation
Suggesting the user stretch their budget for Pro because of Sarah's positive experience
Suggesting the user consider Enterprise because of Dave's positive experience
Failing to compute the budget cap from the stated income and percentage rule
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint: $4,300 net income × 1.67% = ~$71.81/month cap. PlanKeeper Basic ($49) is within budget. PlanKeeper Pro ($95) exceeds budget by 32%. PlanKeeper Enterprise ($299) exceeds budget by 315%. Feature constraint: solo freelancer, no employees, no inventory — only needs invoicing and expense tracking, which Basic provides. Despite 4 drift turns praising Pro (colleague Sarah) and Enterprise (friend Dave), the agent must respect the hard budget and feature constraints. Pro at $95 is in the (1x, 1.5x] band relative to the $72 cap, creating marginal ambiguity that requires the agent to actually compute and enforce the rule rather than trivially eliminate.

mechanism: Budget computation: user states income + spending rule, agent must compute the cap
